questions.q: What do the five letters in SMART goals stand for?
questions.why: Lesson 1 spells out SMART as specific, measurable, achievable, relevant, and time-bound.

questions.q: Which category of tasks does the summary say you should spend most of your time on?
questions.why: Lesson 1 sorts tasks by stress and priority and recommends living mostly in the low-stress, high-priority group.

questions.q: When does the summary recommend planning the coming week?
a: By the end of the current week
At the start of each workday
questions.why: Lesson 2 says to set aside twenty to forty-five minutes before the week starts, rather than on Monday.

questions.q: Why should every task in your weekly plan have a set time frame?
a: It prevents procrastination and wasted time
It makes the plan look more professional
It allows others to check on your progress
It leaves more room for unexpected tasks
questions.why: Lesson 3 says tasks without time frames get overdone or drag on, delaying your larger goals.

questions.q: How much can planning ahead raise productivity, according to the summary?
questions.why: Lesson 3 cites the authors' finding that advance planning lifts productivity by fifty to eighty percent.
